summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and StrataCore focusing on cloud/GPU integration, reseller/managed services model, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and next steps to run benchmarks and schedule a technical deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-14 15:00 PDT | Duration 42m | Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Romero (Redwood SE), Lena Park (StrataCore Head of Partnerships), Marco Giordano (StrataCore Cloud Solutions Architect), Priya Singh (StrataCore GTM)

00:00 Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um we can do quick intros — I'm Ava, AE at Redwood. Diego's our solutions engineer.
00:12 Lena Park: Hi Ava hi Diego, this is Lena, head of partnerships at StrataCore. happy to be here.
00:18 Diego Romero: hey Lena, nice to meet you.
00:20 Marco Giordano: Marco here, cloud infra. we'll talk specifics on the GPU side.
00:25 Priya Singh: and I'm Priya, I run partnerships ops, will be around for GTM questions.
00:30 Ava Chen: Great. Agenda — quick two-minute intros, then we're curious about StrataCore's partner model and target customers, talk integration surface (APIs, private deployments, resale), security questions, then next steps.
00:45 Lena Park: Sounds good. to give quick context — StrataCore is a managed cloud provider focusing on enterprise GPU workloads and verticals like finance and genomics. we also white-label for systems integrators. We're exploring strategic partnerships for inference runtimes to offer to our customers.
01:05 Ava Chen: Awesome. can you tell us where you're currently with inference stacks? are you building in-house, using vendor runtimes, or reselling partners?
01:15 Marco Giordano: Right now most customers run on a mix. some use vendor-managed endpoints (they call AWS/Azure) others self-host an open-source runtime. performance and ops are a headache — kv cache management, batching, and latencies vary a lot. We want a consistent option to offer.
01:35 Diego Romero: totally. that's exactly where Redwood sits — unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, private. curious — what's the primary friction you're hearing from customers?
01:45 Marco Giordano: two big ones: cost predictability (telescoping token costs) and reliability when pushing 8k+ context lengths. Second is compliance — data residency, KMS, and audit logs for regulated customers.
02:00 Ava Chen: Understood. we have Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) options plus KMS integrations and audit logging. For high sequence lengths our kernel selection and batching strategies help; Diego can speak to specifics.
02:13 Diego Romero: yeah — on the runtime side we do continuous batching and KV prefix caching; we also support quantized variants for cost savings. For 8k to 32k contexts we select specialized kernels and route clients to model variants if needed. some of that depends on model family.
02:28 Marco Giordano: when you say route, is that automatic? we need deterministic behavior for SLAs.
02:35 Diego Romero: it's policy-driven. customers can set routing rules by latency SLO, cost tier, or region. also automatic fallback to compatible variants if a variant is out of capacity. you can pin model versions and rollouts.
02:48 Priya Singh: from the GTM side, what does a partner integration look like? reseller license, co-managed, or white-label?
02:56 Ava Chen: we do a mix. common patterns: 1) referral + engineering support; 2) dedicated OEM/resale with partner pricing; 3) larger partnerships where we co-manage Dedicated clusters and provide joint SLAs. We also have partner enablement — docs, onboarding, and benchmark artifacts.
03:14 Lena Park: For StrataCore we like the co-managed model because we run managed services. commercial question — is there an MRR or commit expected for Dedicated?
03:23 Ava Chen: Dedicated is typically commit-based (monthly/annual). there are flexible burst options for spiky workloads. pricing and minimums depend on region and hardware profile. we'll share a sample pricing sheet.
03:33 Marco Giordano: technical question — network egress and VPC peering. can Redwood operate inside our customers' VPCs or do you use a control plane that requires outbound connectivity?
03:43 Diego Romero: our Private deployment supports a customer-managed control plane with VPC peering and private connectivity. for strict air-gapped customers we also have an on-prem package. the hosted API obviously routes through Redwood's control plane but we have region isolation and data retention controls.
03:57 Marco Giordano: okay good. encryption — does Redwood support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and per-tenant key separation?
04:06 Ava Chen: yes, KMS integrations are supported. we can do per-tenant keys in Private and Dedicated setups; hosted can integrate with your KMS in most enterprise tiers.
04:16 Priya Singh: what's your SOC2/ISO status? customers ask.
04:19 Ava Chen: we're SOC2 Type II certified and pursuing ISO 27001; we'll share the certs and security whitepaper after the call.
04:28 Lena Park: perfect. can you run us through a rough benchmark run — we want to see throughput and latency for 13B and 70B models on A100-ish hardware.
04:38 Diego Romero: yes, we typically run latency p95, throughput at different batch sizes, and cost per 1k tokens. For a preliminary run we'd need model versions, sequence length distribution, and sample prompts. we can provision a short Dedicated trial cluster.
04:53 Marco Giordano: timeline wise we'd like a benchmark before the end of the quarter. is that feasible?
04:57 Diego Romero: feasible, yes. we'll need two weeks to set up tests once we get access and test data.
05:05 Ava Chen: let's lock a date for the SE deep dive. does Oct 1 at 10am PT work?
05:11 Marco Giordano: Oct 1 works for me.
05:13 Priya Singh: works for me too.
05:15 Lena Park: yep.
05:17 Ava Chen: Great — Diego will lead technical session.
05:20 Diego Romero: quick technical note — we have some model-specific kernel optimizations that perform differently on Ampere vs Hopper architectures. if you have specific SKUs we should match them.
05:32 Marco Giordano: StrataCore often uses Ampere in some regions and Hopper in our newest clusters. we can provide the exact SKUs.
05:40 Diego Romero: perfect, please share SKUs. also we'd like sample payloads to replicate tokenization distribution.
05:48 Marco Giordano: noted.
05:50 Priya Singh: switching back to partnership commercial — what's the partner enablement like — joint case studies, co-marketing?
05:58 Ava Chen: we offer partner GTM kits, co-marketing credits on enterprise deals, and joint case study templates. for white-label/resale we have an onboarding bundle and a partner portal.
06:09 Lena Park: good. compliance and support SLAs — how do escalations work for co-managed customers?
06:17 Ava Chen: we have tiered support. for Dedicated customers there's an SLA and a designated solutions engineer. in co-managed scenarios we set up runbooks and an escalation path with a named SE.
06:28 Marco Giordano: any audit logging granularity? we need token-level logs but with masking for PII.
06:35 Diego Romero: yes audit logs capture request/response metadata; content logging can be configured and PII masking can be enabled — part of the compliance package.
06:46 Priya Singh: do you have examples of reseller deals or partner success stories?
06:51 Ava Chen: yes — we'll share two short partner success briefs (one with a cloud reseller, one with a fintech customer).
06:58 Lena Park: thanks. any integration work required on our side to onboard customers?
07:04 Diego Romero: depends on pattern. if you're reselling Hosted API it's minimal. for Dedicated or Private there's a setup window — networking, VPC peering, IAM roles, and optionally KMS setup. we provide IaC templates.
07:18 Marco Giordano: IaC is helpful — do you have Terraform modules?
07:21 Diego Romero: we provide Terraform and Helm charts for on-prem and cloud.
07:26 Priya Singh: procurement/legal — any partner agreement terms we should be aware of up-front?
07:31 Ava Chen: standard partner MSA and SOW for services. we can share a template redlines deck. nothing unusually restrictive.
07:38 Lena Park: great. question on pricing model for co-managed Dedicated — is there an uplift for white-labeling?
07:45 Ava Chen: typically partner discount tiers are applied; white-label arrangements have different revenue share models — we'll go into details in commercial discussions.
07:55 Marco Giordano: technical question — do you support GPU telemetry and health metrics for our stack? we need to surface GPU memory patterns to customers.
08:05 Diego Romero: yes we export GPU metrics, per-request latencies, KV cache hit rates, and we surface those in the Redwood Console. you can forward metrics to your monitoring stack (Prometheus, Datadog).
08:18 Priya Singh: any blockers you foresee for a pilot with one of our reference customers?
08:25 Diego Romero: main blockers would be access to test SKUs, sample workloads, and any strict network policies on the customer side. otherwise we can usually spin a trial cluster.
08:36 Lena Park: we'll coordinate.
08:38 Ava Chen: good. another question — do you have preferred legal/compliance questionnaires (SIG, CAIQ)?
08:44 Lena Park: yes we often need CAIQ and sometimes SIG.
08:49 Ava Chen: we can provide our completed CAIQ and security pack.
08:53 Marco Giordano: good. switching to integration ops — do you have a preferred onboarding timeline?
08:58 Ava Chen: typical onboarding for Dedicated co-managed is 4-8 weeks depending on approvals and network setup. simple hosted referrals can be minutes to days.
09:08 Priya Singh: who internally will be the partner success contact on your side?
09:12 Ava Chen: I'll be primary partner contact and Diego will run technical onboarding; we can also introduce our partner success manager if deal progresses.
09:21 Lena Park: sounds good.
09:23 Ava Chen: quick recap of next steps: I'll send the partner one-pager, pricing sheet, and security docs; Diego will draft the benchmark plan; Marco will confirm SKUs and test data; Lena will send StrataCore onboarding checklist. We'll schedule the SE deep dive Oct 1 at 10am PT.
09:42 Marco Giordano: confirmed.
09:44 Priya Singh: confirmed.
09:45 Lena Park: confirmed.
09:47 Ava Chen: Great. any final quick Qs?
09:50 Marco Giordano: none from me.
09:52 Priya Singh: all good.
09:54 Lena Park: thanks everyone.
10:00 Ava Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite.
10:06 (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains small mis-hearings in model family names and SKUs. Shared artifacts mentioned: partner-deck.pdf (link to be shared), security-pack.zip (SOC2 certs, CAIQ), preliminary-benchmark-plan.xlsx.

End of transcript.
